title: National park properties command 24% price premium
summary:
Properties in UK national parks command a 24% price premium compared to similar homes elsewhere, with the New Forest averaging £563,000. National landscapes show a 14% premium, according to Nationwide Building Society research.

title: Permitted development conversions face finance gap
summary:
A mismatch between permitted development rights and available finance products has created challenges for landlords seeking to convert commercial properties into residential units. Class MA permitted development rights allow conversions without full planning applications, but lenders' assessment criteria have not fully adapted to this borrower category.

The post Permitted development conversions face finance gap appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Period properties listed across England and Scotland
summary:
Five period properties with distinctive architectural features have been listed for sale across England and Scotland, with asking prices ranging from £525,000 to £1.15 million. The listings include Victorian homes in Ipswich, York, Nottinghamshire, London and a coastal cottage in Fife.

title: Tenants spend third of income on rent as prices rise 4.3%
summary:
Tenants in the UK are spending 32.7% of their annual income on rent, according to new research from Lomond, as average monthly rents reach £1,369. The data shows average monthly rent has increased 4.3% year-on-year, continuing an upward trend in the rental market.

title: Landlord exodus warning as sector faces regulatory pressure
summary:
Rising operational costs and increased regulation are driving landlords to exit the private rental sector, according to warnings from industry figures. The caution comes as Office for National Statistics figures show rents increased 3.7% in the year to July 2026.

title: Proptech firm iamproperty joins Open Property Data Association
summary:
Proptech firm iamproperty has joined the Open Property Data Association, becoming part of an industry-wide initiative to standardise property information across UK transactions. The company will support the development of open data standards aimed at reducing friction in the home buying and selling process.

title: Rent control debate intensifies as IFS warns of supply risks
summary:
Housing Secretary Angela Rayner faces pressure from 26 MPs to introduce rent controls, despite IFS warnings that such measures could reduce housing supply and push down property prices. The government has confirmed it has no plans to implement rent controls.

The post Rent control debate intensifies as IFS warns of supply risks appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Pet ownership drives homebuying decisions, new data shows
summary:
One in ten prospective homebuyers in the UK is seeking to purchase property specifically to own a pet, according to new research from Skipton Building Society. The lender's data reveals that an additional 11% of buyers are actively searching for pet-friendly properties.

title: Limited company structures now account for 45% of BTL ownership
summary:
Limited company ownership now accounts for 45.1% of buy-to-let properties in the UK, with the structure becoming the dominant model among landlords with larger portfolios. Analysis shows that for landlords with 20 or more properties, 57.6% now operate through limited company structures.

title: Lettings agent falsely claimed industry membership
summary:
A Birmingham-based lettings agent accused of withholding tenant deposits and failing to pass rent to landlords has been found falsely presenting himself as a member of Propertymark, the industry trade body.
